author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, all on one page. The page has no navigation entry and no inbound link; its own address is the only way in.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then every one of them is listed by its stored name
given a specialty that veterinarians hold, when the specialty directory is opened, then each holder is listed under it by first name and last name
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears nowhere on the page
given more specialties than the veterinarian directory would show on one page, when the specialty directory is opened, then all of them are listed together, without paging
given the specialty directory's address, when it is requested directly, then the page is served, and no other page links to it
edge case 1: a specialty that no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian shown under it
edge case 2: when the clinic knows no specialties at all, the page still renders rather than failing
edge case 3: specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are listed in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one
edge case 4: a specialty's stored name is data rather than interface wording, so it is shown as stored in every supported language
non_goals: a navigation entry or a link from any other page to the specialty directory - deliberate scope for this request, possible follow-up
managing veterinarians or their specialties (NG-2, unchanged)
notes: The page's address is /specialties.html, stated by the product owner; with no navigation entry it is the whole entry point. The Non-Goals table is unchanged, so no scope_overrides are carried: NG-2 stands as written and the missing entry point is recorded as an open question, not a new non-goal. Two open questions were recorded in docs/prd.md instead of consulting, per the dispatch: whether the page should get a visible entry point, and which key orders the listing (the requirement fixes only that the order is stable).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice is a second read-only HTTP surface on the existing vet feature package, built from patterns already in force: Repository, Web controller, and a Thymeleaf template under templates/vets composed with fragments/layout. One small addition is needed. No repository reads Specialty today, and edge case 1 (a specialty no veterinarian holds) cannot be satisfied from VetRepository.findAll() alone, because that path only reaches specialties reachable through a vet. Add SpecialtyRepository in the vet package, mirroring PetTypeRepository: a Spring Data interface over a lookup value type. No new module, no new pattern, no new dependency, no change to the persistence mapping. The dependency graph is unchanged (vet still depends only on model). See docs/system-design.md sections Package Structure and Contracts, and docs/adr/2026-07-31-feature-package-organization.md and docs/adr/2026-07-31-server-side-rendering-with-thymeleaf.md.
integration_points: VetController gains a second GET mapping at /specialties.html, alongside the existing /vets.html and /vets routes; it injects SpecialtyRepository in addition to VetRepository
SpecialtyRepository is a new Spring Data interface over the existing specialties table; no schema change, no data.sql change, no new cache
VetRepository.findAll() is reused unchanged as the veterinarian source; Vet.getSpecialties() is already EAGER, so the read works with spring.jpa.open-in-view disabled
The new template composes fragments/layout, so the page carries site-wide navigation per REQ-SYS-001 without a navigation entry of its own
Message keys already present (specialties, vets, name, none) cover the page chrome; no new key is expected

patterns.description: Repository over a lookup value type in a feature package - the precedent SpecialtyRepository follows. Prefer VetRepository's narrower base (Repository<Specialty, Integer> with a single read method and @Transactional(readOnly = true)) over JpaRepository, per architecture-principles.md Minimal surface
The existing vet-directory read: GET mapping, repository read, model attribute, view name returned. The specialty directory follows the same shape minus the pagination helper
Layout composition and table rendering. Copy the layout call and the th:each/th:text discipline; drop the pagination block entirely (no paging is an acceptance criterion)
Established resource-walking test shape. The 'no other page links to it' criterion is testable the same way: walk src/main/resources/templates and assert /specialties.html appears in no template

risks.risk: Grouping veterinarians under specialties lands in VetController, adding a new rule to a web controller. architecture-principles.md Design Validation Checklist bars this, and states the existing controller deviation does not extend to new rules
risks.mitigation: Put the projection in SpecialtyDirectory, an immutable value object in the vet package with a static factory taking the specialties and the veterinarians as arguments. VetController fetches, delegates, adds one model attribute, returns the view name. SpecialtyDirectory is unit-testable with real Specialty and Vet objects and no Spring context, which is where the four edge cases belong

risks.risk: Ordering by SQL ORDER BY makes the listing order vendor-dependent. The PostgreSQL owner-search defect in docs/system-design.md Known Defects is the precedent: the three vendor schemas do not agree on collation, so the same query orders differently per database
risks.mitigation: Impose the total order in SpecialtyDirectory with explicit comparators, not in the repository query. Keep SpecialtyRepository's read unordered

risks.risk: All specialties on one page is unbounded by construction; a large specialty table would render one very large page
risks.mitigation: Accepted by REQ-VET-003, which rules out paging. The seeded set is three specialties. Revisit only if the count grows

risks.risk: A new message key silently breaks REQ-LANG-002 if it is not added to all eleven bundles
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing keys (specialties, vets, name, none). If a new key is unavoidable, add it to messages.properties and all ten locale bundles; I18nPropertiesSyncTest also rejects literal HTML text without th:text or #{}

notes: Design decisions taken here, so the implementer does not have to guess. (1) Listing order - the PRD Open Questions entry asking which key orders the listing is resolved as a design decision: specialties by stored name ascending, case-insensitive, with entity id as final tiebreaker; veterinarians under each specialty by last name, then first name, then id. Both comparators live in SpecialtyDirectory and are asserted directly in its unit test. docs/prd.md is not mine to edit - product-requirements-expert can close that open question against this record. (2) Specialty holders are read by joining in memory, not by adding an inverse @ManyToMany to Specialty. Vet already owns the association and fetches it EAGER, so the join needs no mapping change and no lazy-loading concession under open-in-view disabled. (3) SpecialtyDirectory carries plain strings - the specialty name, and each holder's full name composed first-then-last - rather than Vet references. Composing the full name inside the tested value object is the stronger placement, because 'first name before last name' is a requirement statement rather than presentation. This differs deliberately from vetList.html, which concatenates in the template; the value object must satisfy the Domain Core properties in full, and the persistence-entity exception does not cover it. (4) SpecialtyRepository is not cached. CacheConfiguration declares only the vets cache, and cache eviction is an unresolved open question in docs/system-design.md; adding a second cache would extend an open problem for no stated need. (5) Layout menu argument - pass a value that matches no navigation item (for example 'specialties'), not 'vets'. fragments/layout.html highlights only when active == menu, so an unmatched value renders full navigation with no active item, which is exactly right for a page absent from navigation. (6) No ADR. Every decision above is small and reversible, and each instantiates a catalogued pattern rather than departing from one; none meets the hard-to-reverse-plus-real-trade-off bar. (7) Slice size - one behavior, one route, one template, two new small types, one controller method. Correctly sized; no split, no refactor-first. (8) Security - the route takes no parameter and writes nothing, so it introduces no new trust boundary beyond the unauthenticated-read posture already recorded in docs/system-design.md Security Context. Specialty names and veterinarian names are rendered through th:text, which Thymeleaf escapes by default. (9) docs/system-design.md is deliberately not edited at triage, because it states current state only and this code does not exist yet. Once the slice lands, its Contracts table needs two rows - SpecialtyRepository and SpecialtyDirectory - and REQ-VET-003 added to the VetController row. (10) No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: The Threat Model's cross-site-scripting row scopes rendered user data to 'Owner, pet, and visit fields'. REQ-VET-003 adds a third rendered surface (specialty names and veterinarian full names at /specialties.html). The mitigation is unchanged and correct - Thymeleaf default escaping - so this is a documentation-accuracy point, not a defect: the row's attack-vector column now understates the surface it covers. No security consequence for this change set.

approved_aspects: Output escaping: every value in src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html renders through th:text - the specialty name (${entry.name}) and each holder full name (${holder + ' '}). No th:utext, th:inline, th:attr, th:href, th:src, or DOM injection appears in the new template; a repository-wide sweep of src/main/resources/templates confirms th:utext and th:inline occur nowhere, so no instance of the unescaped-output class exists. Thymeleaf default escaping is not disabled anywhere, matching docs/security-principles.md Realization and the Threat Model's XSS row. Stored specialty and veterinarian names carrying markup render inert.

Injection surface: SpecialtyRepository.findAll() is a Spring Data derived query on Repository<Specialty, Integer> with no @Query, no native SQL, and no string-concatenated predicate. VetRepository.findAll() is reused unchanged. No SQL, JPQL, or SpEL expression in the change set is composed from caller-supplied text.

No request-derived input: GET /specialties.html declares no @RequestParam, @PathVariable, @ModelAttribute, or request body - the handler takes only Model. There is therefore no binder to configure, so the mass-assignment / identifier-tampering control (setDisallowedFields) has no applicable surface here, and no path-traversal or resource-resolution vector is introduced. The change adds no write path, no file I/O, no deserialization entry point, and no outbound connection.

Secrets: a scan of the change set for credential-shaped material (token, password, secret, key, credential, connection strings, URLs) returns only the Apache license header URL and the Thymeleaf namespace URI. No credential, connection string, or identifier reaches a log line, an exception message, or the rendered page.

Data exposure: the endpoint is unauthenticated, consistent with the application-wide absence of authentication already recorded in docs/system-design.md Security Context. It discloses no data class not already public - veterinarian names and their specialties are served today by GET /vets.html and the GET /vets JSON endpoint. The specialty directory is a re-projection of that same set, so it opens no new disclosure class. The absence of an inbound link is PRD scope, not relied on as an access control.

Unbounded read: SpecialtyRepository.findAll() and VetRepository.findAll() are both unpaged, and the page renders every row. The exposure is a response-size / memory concern only - it carries no authorization, injection, or disclosure consequence, is bounded by operator-controlled seeded data rather than by any caller input (no parameter can amplify it), and the identical unpaged VetRepository.findAll() already backs GET /vets. REQ-VET-003 rules out paging explicitly and the design record accepts the size risk against a three-row seeded table. Not a security finding; flagged here so the acceptance is on the record.

Supply chain: build.gradle and the dependency set are untouched by the change set (git status shows no build-file modification), so no new artifact, transitive edge, or CVE surface is introduced and no version-bump verification applies. The change uses only Spring Boot 4.1.0 components already present.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The test name and PRD edge case 4 both claim 'every supported language', but the body sends Accept-Language: de exactly once and never touches the other nine bundles under src/main/resources/messages (en, es, fa, hi, ja, ko, pt, ru, tr). The mechanism (th:text on the raw entity field, no message key) is locale-independent, so one locale is enough evidence the assertion holds, but the test as named over-claims what it checked, and a reader debugging a future regression in one specific bundle (e.g. the RTL fa bundle) gets no signal from this suite either way.
findings.fix: Either parameterize with @ParameterizedTest/@ValueSource over a representative sample of the locale codes (including a non-Latin one, e.g. ja or fa) and assert the stored name is unchanged under each, or rename the test to state what it actually verifies (e.g. theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowAStoredNameUnchangedUnderANonDefaultLocale) so the name stops overclaiming.

findings.description: One test asserts two unrelated concerns: SpecialtyDirectory.of(null, ...) rejecting a null specialties collection, and SpecialtyDirectory.of(..., null) rejecting a null veterinarians collection. testing-principles.md Assertions says multiple assertions on the same result are fine but testing unrelated concerns is not - these are two different parameters failing independently, not one result inspected twice.
findings.fix: Split into two tests, e.g. theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRejectMissingSpecialties and theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRejectMissingVeterinarians, or drive both cases through one @ParameterizedTest with the varying argument and expected message as parameters.

approved_aspects: All four prd.md edge cases have dedicated, substantive tests: EC1 (a holder-less specialty still listed) in theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListASpecialtyNoVeterinarianHolds, EC2 (empty specialty set still renders) covered at both the unit level and, more strongly, through a real MockMvc + Thymeleaf render in theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderWhenNoSpecialtyExists, EC3 (stable order) covered thoroughly - name ordering, case-insensitivity, id tie-break, and holder last-name/first-name ordering are each asserted with deliberately chosen non-monotonic ids/names that would fail under an accidental-order implementation, EC4 partially covered (see autofix finding)

SpecialtyDirectory is tested with real Vet/Specialty objects and no Spring context, matching the design block's placement rationale and the brief's real-objects-first mocking policy; VetControllerTests uses the sole sanctioned mock (MockMvc/@WebMvcTest) plus the pre-existing VetRepository mock precedent for the new SpecialtyRepository, not a new mocking pattern
